cards.title: Introduction to Type Hints
cards.content:
Python is dynamically typed, but since PEP 484, you can use type hints (or type annotations) to specify the expected data types of variables, function arguments, and return values.

def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}"

Note that Python at runtime does not enforce these types. They are primarily used by static type checkers like mypy, IDEs, and linters to catch bugs early.

cards.title: Collections and Generics
cards.content:
When annotating collections like lists, dictionaries, or tuples, you specify the container type and the types of its elements.

from typing import List, Dict, Tuple

# A list of strings
names: List[str] = ["Alice", "Bob"]

# A dictionary mapping strings to integers
scores: Dict[str, int] = {"Alice": 95, "Bob": 87}

# A tuple with fixed types
point: Tuple[int, int] = (10, 20)

Tip: In Python 3.9+, you can use built-in types directly (e.g., list[str], dict[str, int]) without importing from the typing module.

cards.title: Optional, Union, and Any
cards.content:
Real-world code often deals with variables that can hold multiple types or might be None.

  • Union: Value can be one of several types. (e.g., Union[int, str])
  • Optional: Value can be a specific type or None. Equivalent to Union[T, None].
  • Any: Disables type checking for that value (escape hatch).
from typing import Optional, Union

def process_id(user_id: Union[int, str]) -> Optional[str]:
    if not user_id:
        return None
    return str(user_id)

cards.title: Type Aliases and Protocols
cards.content:
As codebases grow, complex types can become hard to read. You can create Type Aliases to simplify them.

from typing import Dict, List

# Type Alias
Vector = List[float]

def scale(scalar: float, vector: Vector) -> Vector:
    return [scalar * num for num in vector]

Python also supports structural subtyping via Protocols (duck typing with static types), allowing you to define interfaces based on methods rather than explicit inheritance.

Configure a static type checker like mypy (e.g., mypy.ini).
Run the type checker in your CI/CD pipeline or terminal.
Fix any type mismatch errors reported by the checker.
